title: Seeded Poisson Factorization: leveraging domain knowledge to fit topic models
task: Guided topic modelling and seed-based text classification
problem: Unsupervised topic models do not align with predefined concepts; guided alternatives (KeyATM, SeededLDA) are slow.
architecture: Poisson factorisation with Gamma priors whose topic-term rates are raised a priori for seed words of each topic (seeded plus unseeded intensity); variational inference with stochastic gradient optimisation; documents classified by a Naive Bayes classifier on inferred topic intensities.

datasets.name: Amazon customer feedback
datasets.details: six product categories (e.g. Toys 8 092, Health 6 938, Grocery 2 471 reviews)

key_results: Amazon, 30k documents: accuracy 0.73 in 1:07 min vs KeyATM 0.73 in 5:27 and SeededLDA 0.65 in 3:35.
Amazon, 1k documents: accuracy 0.63 vs KeyATM 0.29 and SeededLDA 0.58.
Benchmarks: accuracy 0.60-0.84 vs 0.02-0.39 for unseeded PF; PF sometimes has higher NPMI/UMass (e.g. Banking NPMI 0.12 vs 0.03).
strengths: Fast, scalable guided model that stays robust to imperfect seed words.
Explicit run-time and corpus-size comparisons with guided LDA variants.

limitations.text: Seeding trades some coherence/diversity for classification alignment.
Evaluation focuses on classification; no comparison with neural or embedding topic models.
